title: GPU rollforward activation checklist — NA / EU / APAC
content:
Objective:
Enable staggered activation of GPU capacity (rollforward) across NA, EU, and APAC cloud regions with minimal customer impact and validated performance characteristics. This doc is an operational checklist + timeline + gating criteria for the Q1 2028 rollforward window.

Context and high-level assumptions:
- Target timeframe: Jan 2028 — Mar 2028 (three waves). Dates below are target windows; exact days will be scheduled in the fortnightly ops sync.
- Procurement lead times and cloud quota requests have been submitted; assume soft confirmation for initial capacity by 2027-12-20.
- All numbers call out GPU equivalent slots in our internal "A100-1x-eq" baseline to normalize across instance types/brands/quantization.
- Utilization targets are conservative for first 4 weeks post-activation to allow warm-up and tuning.
- Must validate model kernel selection and fallback variants before moving to next region.

Regional plan summary (wave plan):
- Wave 1 (NA) — Activation window: 2028-01-08 to 2028-01-21.
  - Target capacity online: 2,000 A100-eq slots (baseline mix: 60% p4d-like, 40% a10/rtx variants).
  - Initial steady-state utilization target: 35% token-hour on average first 14 days, ramp to 60% by day 30.
  - Primary objectives: validate request routing, KV cache warm-up behavior, autoscaler headroom.

- Wave 2 (EU) — Activation window: 2028-02-05 to 2028-02-18.
  - Target capacity online: 800 A100-eq slots.
  - Initial steady-state utilization target: 30% then ramp to 55% by day 30.
  - Primary objectives: regional load balancing, fallbacks to NA, cross-region latency heatmaps.

- Wave 3 (APAC) — Activation window: 2028-03-04 to 2028-03-18.
  - Target capacity online: 600 A100-eq slots.
  - Initial steady-state utilization target: 25% ramping to 50% by day 30.
  - Primary objectives: VPC/private network validations, KMS/HSM key access checks, time-zone operational coverage.

Gating criteria to proceed between waves (must be explicitly checked and signed off):
1) Service-level smoke tests: stable generation latency p50/p95 within 10% of lab benchmarks for common sequence lengths (16/128/512).
2) Error rate: 5xx rate <= 0.05% sustained for 48 hours in the newly activated region.
3) Autoscaler behavior: cold-start token latency < baseline threshold for 95% traffic within configured burst windows; no queue growth > 5% of active pool for 72 hours.
4) Cost anomaly checks: spend per token within expected range (±8%) and no runaway spot replacement costs.
5) Observability: trace context, token-level cost attribution, and rollout dashboard widgets reporting correctly for the new region.
6) Security/compliance: KMS access verification and audit logs present for all test operations (EU and APAC waves specifically).

Activation runbook (high-level steps):
Pre-activation (T-21 to T-3 days):
- Confirm cloud quotas and reservation confirmations (ops-quotas team).
- Complete AMI/container bake for target model variants and optimized kernels.
- Pre-provision load-test harnesses with synthetic traffic (per-region).
- Finalize autoscaler policies and queue backpressure thresholds.
- Create targeted canary route (1% traffic) and a dark pool for soak tests.

D-Day activation (Day 0):
- Step 1: Provision node pool and attach to cluster/fleet. Tag nodes with rollforward wave id and owner.
- Step 2: Boot health probes and run quick kernel verification suite (script: infra/scripts/kernel-check.sh --region=<r>).
- Step 3: Bring up router route pinned to new pool with 0.5% canary traffic for 2 hours. Monitor traces/latency/error.
- Step 4: Expand canary to 5% for 4 hours if no regressions.
- Step 5: Open autoscaler to target capacity but keep admission controller conservative for 12 hours.
- Step 6: Enable KV/prefix cache population from warm-up harness; verify hit-rate > 60% within 24 hours.

Post-activation (Day 1–30):
- Continuous monitoring: p50/p95 latency, token throughput, 5xx rate, memory/PCI-e error counters.
- Daily ops checklist items to tick off and record (see checklist section).
- If regressions are detected, hit rollback criteria (see below).

Rollback criteria (immediate rollback triggers):
- Sustained 5xx rate > 0.2% for 1 hour OR > 0.5% for 10 minutes.
- Latency p95 increase > 40% vs pre-activation baseline for 30 minutes.
- Autoscaler instability causing node churn > 10% of pool in 1 hour.
- Security incident or KMS access failure.
Rollback procedure (if triggered):
- Step R1: Re-route traffic off new pool to fallback pools/regions (router: tag-route rollback-wave=<id>).
- Step R2: Drain and cordon nodes; collect diagnostics (dmesg, nvml logs, kube events).
- Step R3: Create hot issue on JIRA INFRA-ROLLBACK-<wave>-<date> and page infra-oncall and SRE.
- Step R4: Keep pool offline until root cause analysis completed and signoff given.

Acceptance tests and smoke checks (explicit):
- Generation smoke: run the standard smoke harness for sequence lengths [16,128,512] using production prompt set (script: smoke/generate-smoke.sh --region=<r>).
- Streaming test: open 50 concurrent streaming sessions and validate frame ordering and token continuity.
- KV cache verification: run prefix-population and measure cache hit-rate and token-cost delta.
- Billing attribution: confirm token-level cost shows region label and route id in billing export for 24 hours.

Operational checklist (to mark daily for first 14 days):
- [ ] p50/p95 latency within target
- [ ] 5xx error rate <= 0.05%
- [ ] Autoscaler stable (no sudden scale-to-zero or flapping)
- [ ] KV cache hit-rate trending up
- [ ] Cost per token within expected bounds
- [ ] No GPU/driver hardware alerts
- [ ] Trace sampling linked to last 100 user requests

People and paging matrix:
- Wave owner: Marin Okafor (owner on-call during activation windows)
- Infra on-call: Diego Morales (primary), Lina Becker (secondary)
- SRE escalation: Priya Shah (pager after 15 minutes)
- Product incident lead: Alex Nguyen (notify on customer-impacting regressions)
- Pager: #infra-rollouts slack channel + infra-oncall pager duty.

Risk matrix (high level):
- Risk: Cloud quota delays -> Mitigation: maintain pre-approved soft reservations and parallel fallback to different instance type with similar performance profile.
- Risk: Kernel regressions with quantized models -> Mitigation: rapid revert pipeline and pre-activation kernel validation harness.
- Risk: Unexpected cost spikes -> Mitigation: hard spend guardrails and automated throttles on non-critical routes.

Quick math (capacity delta and warm buffer):
- NA: 2,000 slots * expected avg active fraction 0.35 -> ~700 active at day0. Warm buffer: keep 200 extra slots for autoscaler headroom.
- EU: 800 slots -> ~240 active at day0; buffer 80 slots.
- APAC: 600 slots -> ~150–180 active at day0; buffer 60 slots.

Open action items (owners):
- [Marin] finalize canary routing rules and minimal exposure plan (due 2026-11-22).
- [Diego] complete kernel-check automation and baking into CICD (PR posted; need review).
- [Priya] validate KMS access patterns for APAC regions and run audit mock (due 2026-11-30).
- [Lina] coordinate with procurement to confirm spot/commit mix and fallback SKUs (due 2026-11-25).

Notes / references / links:
- Quick test commands: infra/scripts/kernel-check.sh, smoke/generate-smoke.sh, infra/scripts/region-cost-checker.py
- Related Jira: INFRA-1429, INFRA-1502 (kernel bake), INFRA-1518 (billing tagging).
- Confluence runbook: confluence:redwood-infra/gpu-rollforward-2028

Appendix (sample daily log template):
- date:
- window (wave):
- capacity provisioned:
- p50/p95 latency:
- 5xx rate:
- autoscaler events (count):
- cost-per-token (24h):
- notes/actions:

This is a living doc; update as we learn from each wave. The goal is a repeatable, low-drag activation pattern we can hand to partners and downstream platform teams.
